datasets.name: uci-heart-failure-clinical
datasets.prediction_time: Recorded death during the supplied follow-up from clinical measurements. Follow-up time is excluded as outcome-associated information; no uniform survival horizon or clinical deployment claim.

target_timing_review.task: Retrospective classification of the supplied patient-record outcome, with follow-up duration excluded; NOT an all-fields outcome classifier or an established baseline prognostic model.
target_timing_review.endpoint: death_event=1 means death occurred during that patient's recorded follow-up; 0 means no recorded death during that observation period, not indefinite survival.
target_timing_review.predictor_timing_limit: The primary dataset describes records collected during follow-up. Removing time does not prove every remaining clinical predictor was available at a common baseline; no such availability is claimed.
target_timing_review.survival_analysis_limit: No fixed prediction horizon, common follow-up window, censoring adjustment or time-to-event model is defined by this binary classification recipe.

datasets.name: uci-student-performance
datasets.prediction_time: Recorded final Portuguese-course grade from the school/questionnaire record; G1 and G2 are excluded as other targets. Retrospective association, not an asserted enrollment-time early-warning task.

target_timing_review.task: Retrospective regression of the final Portuguese-course grade from the supplied school/questionnaire record, WITHOUT prior-period grade predictors.
target_timing_review.endpoint: G3 is the final-year grade issued at the third period, on the original 0-20 scale.
target_timing_review.predictor_timing_limit: Remaining predictors include recorded school absences and questionnaire/school attributes whose availability at enrollment or an earlier term is not established. No enrollment-time or pre-term early-warning claim is made.

- Anomaly: we use the publicly available dataset state, which is without preprocessing. Moreover, we were not able to inverse the original ordinal encoding of the label.
